title: CedarPoint FinOps LLM onramp - personal notes
content:
Meeting: CedarPoint (FinOps) initial technical onramp call - notes and action items
Date: 2024-11-08
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Priya Sharma (CedarPoint lead), Diego Alvarez (CedarPoint infra), Jen Park (CedarPoint security) 
Quick summary: CedarPoint is a mid-market FinOps platform (SaaS) evaluating Redwood to add LLM features for transaction tagging, intent classification, and an in-product assistant for customers. They want predictable cost, strict PII handling, and ability to run private deployments inside their GCP VPC (customer-managed). This doc is my scratchpad from the call + rough requirements, gotchas, token math, and next steps.

Customer context / goals:
- Replace current brittle rules engine for transaction categorization with a taxonomy-aware model (reduce manual tagging load by 60% target).
- Add a contextual assistant to answer billing and usage questions for customers (chat UI inside product).
- Keep sensitive data off public endpoints (no raw PII leaves their VPC).
- Prefer reserved/dedicated capacity (predictable pricing) but want an evaluation POC first.

Technical constraints mentioned:
- Primary cloud: GCP (us-west1 + us-east1). On-prem not required now but may consider private deployment for EU region later.
- Network: strict egress controls, only allow outbound to certain Redwood control-plane endpoints through proxy.
- Auth: SSO via SAML (Okta) + service accounts. Need token rotation and audit logs forwarded to their Splunk instance.
- Data retention: logs must be retained for 90 days; debug traces must be scrubbed of PII before leaving their environment.
- Throughput: spikey traffic during billing runs end of month; baseline ~2 qps, spikes to 40–50 qps for short windows.
- Latency target for assistant flows: p95 <= 600ms for short replies (~<=150 tokens). For batch classification jobs, throughput matters more than latency.

Initial feature mapping / recommendations
- Classification pipeline: run batched classify jobs on Dedicated pool with auto-burst. Use Redwood Optimize suggestions: quantized 8-bit model for cost; maintain a FP16 variant for high-quality fallback.
- Assistant: use hosted streaming API in canary first, then Private VPC when security gating passes. Enable prefix caching for repeated help prompts to reduce tokens.
- KV cache: recommend preloading customer taxonomy as context (small embedding store in their VPC) to avoid repeated full-context sends.
- Rate limiting: set conservative client-side throttles and token-level quotas during POC.

Token/Cost rough math (customer gave sample volume)
- Baseline: 2 qps * 3600 * 24 ~ 172,800 requests/day (but most are background batch; realistic daily active chat requests closer to 20k/day).
- Average classification call: 600 tokens in, 5 tokens out -> ~605 tokens. Daily cost sens estimate: 20k * 605 = 12.1M tokens/day.
- Assistant: average chat session 250 in / 150 out -> 400 tokens/session. Expect 3k sessions/day in POC -> 1.2M tokens/day.
- Combined POC tokens/day ~13.3M tokens -> monthly ~400M tokens. This maps to Dedicated commit sizing discussion. Need to run two-week pilot to validate numbers.

Security / Compliance notes
- They will require an onboarding questionnaire (we sent earlier) to be completed before private deployment. Key asks: KMS integration (customer-managed keys), HSM optional, and audit log forwarding.
- Data scrubbing: must provide a pre-send hook or client-side middleware to strip SSNs/credit-card numbers. They prefer client-side redaction + field-level encryption for customer IDs.
- Legal: contract team flagged additional MDR (data processing addendum) for financial data. Pricing and SLAs contingent on that.

Integration gotchas called out in meeting
- Proxy/NAT: Their outbound egress uses a corporate proxy that does TLS inspection; need to confirm compatibility with our mTLS requirement for private control-plane. Might require tunnels or dedicated NAT exceptions.
- Tokenization: their current logging pipeline splits tokens strangely (unicode normalization issues). Might overcount tokens in our billing estimator. Need sample payloads to re-run estimations.
- Model fallback behavior: they want deterministic fallback (if quantized model confidence < threshold, route to FP16). Need to sketch routing policy for Canary -> Dedicated FP16 fallback.

POC scope (agreed loosely in call)
- 2-week POC: classification batch job + assistant prototype embedded in billing UI.
- Metrics to measure: classification accuracy lift vs baseline (target +60% reduction in manual tagging), average latency (p95), token spend delta vs estimate, and error/retry rate.
- POC environments: staging in their GCP project; Redwood provides temporary canary hosted endpoints and a dedicated small pool in us-west1 for batch.

Open questions (TODOs to resolve)
- Diego to provide sample 1 week of production traffic (anonymized) for token analysis (due 2024-11-13).
- Security: Jen to confirm whether proxy will allow mTLS to Redwood control plane or if we need an IP allowlist (due 2024-11-15).
- Legal: send DPA template and get back with redlines (owner: Maya / Legal) — ask approximate timeline.
- Pricing: table of Dedicated commit tiers we should propose for 400M/month; coordinate with Sales (Liam) for commit model.

Immediate next steps (owners + dates)
- Send two-page POC plan + acceptance criteria to Priya (Maya) — by 2024-11-10.
- Request anonymized traffic dump + example payloads (Maya -> Diego) — due 2024-11-13.
- Run tokenization pass on sample and adjust cost estimate (Liam) — due 2024-11-14.
- Security deep-dive meeting to confirm network/auth integration (invite Redwood infra + CedarPoint infra) — schedule for week of 2024-11-18 (Priya + Diego to propose times).
- Draft a quick-run deployment checklist for Private VPC onboarding (Maya) — by 2024-11-12.

Personal notes / heuristics from call
- Emphasize predictable unit economics (they're a FinOps shop; speak their language: reserved units, committed throughput, predictability vs spot).
- Avoid jargon-heavy claims about model accuracy; show concrete before/after tagging examples.
- For their security folks, be explicit about where PII is redacted (client-side) vs what our audit logs contain.

Rough checklist for POC readiness
- [ ] Anonymized traffic and sample payloads received
- [ ] DPA / MSA handshake in progress
- [ ] Small Dedicated pool provisioned in staging region
- [ ] Client-side redaction middleware prototype added to sample app
- [ ] Tokenization & cost model validated with real payloads
- [ ] Security meeting scheduled and network path validated

Notes epoch: 2024-11-08 17:20 PST — saving quick so SE + Sales can iterate.

Scratchy ideas for follow-up collateral
- One-pager: "How we keep financial PII off the wire" (client-side redaction + KMS + audit flow)
- Slide: "Estimated commit tiers for CedarPoint" with three scenarios: conservative (200M/mo), expected (400M/mo), growth (1B/mo) including cost delta vs pay-as-you-go.
- Mini-demo: show cached taxonomy + assistant answering a billing question with p95 < 500ms (if possible).

End of notes.

-- Maya
